title: Directions and places
title_target: ផ្លូវ និង ទីកន្លែង — phlow neng tii-kan-laeng
goal: Ask for directions and say where things are — and realize that Khmer "prepositions" are really nouns, so "on the table" is literally "at the surface of the table".
bekal: ask for directions with នៅឯណា? and ទៅ … យ៉ាងម៉េច?
use ឆ្វេង, ស្ដាំ, ត្រង់ to give directions
say where things are with លើ, ក្រោម, ក្នុង, ក្រៅ, ខាង
haggle with a tuk-tuk driver and name your destination
give distances in minutes, not kilometers

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — Looking for the post office
dialogs.intro: Ani is lost among Phnom Penh's numbered streets. Notice that almost every place expression in this dialogue starts with ខាង (*khaang*) — a word meaning "side", and the backbone of the whole Khmer system of directions.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [សូមទោស|soum-touh] [ពូ|puu]។ [ប្រៃសណីយ៍|prey-sa-nii] [នៅ|neuw] [ឯណា|'ae-naa] [ចាស|chaah]?
lines.id: Excuse me, uncle. Where is the post office?
lines.literal: sorry — uncle. post — be — where — yes(f)?

lines.speaker: ពូ:
lines.text: [ប្រៃសណីយ៍|prey-sa-nii] [ឬ|reu]? [នៅ|neuw] [ជិត|chit] [ទន្លេ|ton-lé] [បាទ|baat]។
lines.id: The post office? Near the river.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ទៅ|teuw] [ទីនោះ|tii-nuh] [យ៉ាងម៉េច|yaang-méch] [ចាស|chaah]?

lines.speaker: ពូ:
lines.text: [ដើរ|daeu] [ត្រង់|traang] [ទៅ|teuw] [មុខ|muk] [បន្តិច|ban-tech], [រួច|ruèch] [បត់|bat] [ស្ដាំ|sdam] [បាទ|baat]។
lines.id: Go straight ahead a little, then turn right.
lines.literal: walk — straight — go — face — a-little, then — turn — right — yes(m).

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [បត់|bat] [ស្ដាំ|sdam] [នៅ|neuw] [ភ្លើង|phleung] [ស្តុប|sdop] [មែនទេ|mèn-té]?
lines.id: Turn right at the traffic light, right?
lines.literal: turn — right — at — light — stop — right-(question)?

lines.speaker: ពូ:
lines.text: [បាទ|baat]។ [រួច|ruèch] [ដើរ|daeu] [ត្រង់|traang] [ទៀត|tiet]។ [ប្រៃសណីយ៍|prey-sa-nii] [នៅ|neuw] [ខាងឆ្វេង|khaang-chhwéng]។
lines.id: Yes. Then go straight again. The post office is on the left.
lines.literal: yes(m). then — walk — straight — again. post — be — side-left.

lines.speaker: ពូ:
lines.text: [អត់ទេ|'at-té]។ [ដប់|dop] [នាទី|nie-tii] [ដោយ|daoy] [ថ្មើរជើង|thmaeu-cheung] [បាទ|baat]។
lines.literal: no. ten — minute — by — foot-walking — yes(m).

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [អរគុណ|'aa-kun] [ច្រើន|chraeun] [ចាស|chaah]! [ចុះ|choh] [ធនាគារ|thu-nie-kiè] [វិញ|weñ]?
lines.id: Thank you very much! And the bank?
lines.literal: thank-you — much — yes(f)! and-then — bank — in-return?

lines.speaker: ពូ:
lines.text: [ធនាគារ|thu-nie-kiè] [នៅ|neuw] [ខាងក្រោយ|khaang-kraoy] [ផ្សារ|phsaa] [បាទ|baat]។ [ជាប់|choap] [នឹង|neng] [ហាង|haang] [កាហ្វេ|kaa-fé]។
lines.id: The bank is behind the market. Right next to a coffee shop.
lines.literal: bank — be — side-back — market — yes(m). stuck — with — shop — coffee.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [យល់|yual] [ហើយ|haeuy] [ចាស|chaah]។ [អរគុណ|'aa-kun]!

lines.speaker: ពូ:
lines.text: [អត់អីទេ|'at-'ey-té] [បាទ|baat]។ [ដំណើរ|dam-naeu] [ល្អ|l'aa]!
lines.id: You're welcome. Have a good trip!

grammars.title: ⚠️ Khmer "prepositions" are really nouns
body: Khmer has almost no true prepositions. What it uses instead are **nouns that name a part**: លើ means "top surface", ក្រោម means "underside", ក្នុង means "inside". So "on the table" is literally "at the surface of the table".

head: Khmer
Say it
Literally
Meaning
rows: ចន្លោះ … និង …

after: This is actually good news: you don't have to memorize a list of unrelated prepositions, just the names of the parts of things. English does something similar with "in front of", "on top of", "at the back of" — Khmer simply drops the "of".

⚠️ And remember unit 2: នៅ can come before any of them when you want to say "is at" — ​សៀវភៅនៅលើតុ ("the book is on the table"). Without នៅ, សៀវភៅលើតុ means "the book on the table", a phrase, not a sentence.

grammars.title: ខាង — the word that makes every direction
body: ខាង (*khaang*) means "side". Put in front of a direction word, it turns it into a complete place expression. One pattern, a dozen words.
after: ⚠️ Look at **east and west**: ខាងកើត from កើត (to rise) and ខាងលិច from លិច (to sink) — the side where the sun rises and the side where it sets. English "orient" and "occident" come from exactly the same idea (Latin "rising" and "falling"). Once you see it, you'll never mix them up again.

grammars.title: Giving and asking for directions
body: These six verbs make up almost every direction you will hear and give.

head: Key sentence
Say it
Meaning
rows: ទៅ … យ៉ាងម៉េច?
ប៉ុន្មាននាទី?
ខ្ញុំវង្វេងផ្លូវ

after: ⚠️ **Distance in Cambodia is measured in time, not kilometers.** The question ប៉ុន្មានគីឡូម៉ែត្រ? ("how many kilometers?") often gets a useless guess. The question ប៉ុន្មាននាទី? always gets an answer you can use.

blocks.text: Tuk-tuks are the most common way to get around Cambodian cities. The rules are simple: **agree on the price before you get in**, name your destination clearly, and have small change ready in riel.

blocks.title: Why Phnom Penh's streets have numbers
items: **Major odd-numbered streets run north–south, even-numbered ones east–west.** Once you know this you can hardly get lost: if the street numbers go up, you are walking in one fixed direction.

**Cambodians mention landmarks more often than street names.** "Behind the market", "across from the wat", "next to the coffee shop". Learning to name landmarks is far more useful than memorizing street names.
**The river is the biggest landmark.** ទន្លេ (*ton-lé*) means river, and in Phnom Penh it always means the Tonlé Sap riverside. Any tuk-tuk driver will understand it.
